description: Tested: the membrane's evidence registry is hash-chained and verified (ledger + cross-check). Tail truncation: detectable only against a tail anchored outside the ledger, not implemented. Limit: this covers the technical integrity of recorded events. It does not establish complete automatic logging over the system's lifecycle, which Article 12 requires of high-risk AI systems.

evidence.caveat: Covers chain integrity and membrane registry cross-check. Tail truncation is not detected without an externally anchored head, which is not implemented.

source.official_wording: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system.

description: COMMIT_BINDING and SCHEMA_SAFETY are integrity controls, not robustness measures. Article 15(4) requires resilience to errors, faults, and inconsistencies through technical redundancy and fail-safe plans; Article 15(5) requires resilience against unauthorized third-party exploitation. These mechanisms ensure payload integrity and schema conformance, not system robustness or cybersecurity against external attacks. Limit: integrity validation only, not robustness or cybersecurity as required by Art. 15.

source.official_wording: High-risk AI systems shall be as resilient as possible regarding errors, faults or inconsistencies that may occur within the system or the environment in which the system operates.

description: POLICY_ANCHOR is one element of a quality management system, not a QMS itself. Article 17(1) requires providers to put in place a complete QMS documented as written policies, procedures and instructions covering strategy, design control, data management, risk management, record-keeping, post-market monitoring, and more. A policy anchor at start-up is a single integrity check within that system. Limit: one QMS element, not the system required by Art. 17.

source.official_wording: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall put a quality management system in place that ensures compliance with this Regulation.

STRUCTURE_GATE is an admission condition at execution start, not an AI system impact assessment. Clause 6.1.4 requires a formal, documented process evaluating impacts on individuals and societies. The mechanism does not constitute such a process. Limit: admission control only, not an impact assessment.

Clause 8.4 requires a formal, documented process by which impacts on individuals, groups, or societies are identified, evaluated and addressed. An automated veto does not constitute such a process. Re-mapping pending.
